Project: SPACE ORBITAL MECHANICS
Description: It is an interactive desktop space-mission simulator and live planet/moon tracker built in Python for the Space Mission Game.Powered by NASA JPL DE421 . Players act as flight directors managing a $250M budget to launch missions to the Moon and Planets.By balancing payload mass, chemical vs. ion engines, fuel, solar power, and radiation shielding, the game checks real orbital physics, logs scores in MySQL, and animates the Hohmann transfer orbit.
summary: Kepler Space Mission Architect is an interactive Python space game powered by real NASA JPL DE421 planetary data. You play as a flight director managing a $250M budget to launch missions to the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, or Saturn. You choose your payload, engine type, fuel mass, solar power, and radiation shielding. The code then checks real orbital mechanics, delta-v rocket physics, and Kepler's laws to see if your craft survives and reaches its target. Winning flights get saved to a MySQL leaderboard, and a live map animates your spacecraft flying along the curved Hohmann transfer path. You can also check live 3D planet distances anytime.
details:
BENIFITS:

• Uses Real NASA Data: Instead of fake arcade numbers, every launch uses live NASA planetary positions and real physics formulas.

• Learning: It makes complex rocket science and gravitation equations easy to see and test in real time.

• Lightweight & Fast: It runs smoothly on a standard laptop with instant visual feedback and a permanent score tracker.

My goal is to help students and space fans understand how real space missions are planned. By letting anyone act as a mission designer and test real engineering trade-offs—like balancing fuel weight against solar power and radiation shielding .I hope to make orbital mechanics fun and inspire more students to explore aerospace engineering.

TOOLS AND CODING LANGUAGES

• Coding Language: Python

• Libraries & Data: Skyfield (with NASA JPL DE421 planetary ephemeris data), Matplotlib, NumPy, Tkinter, and MySQL Connector

• Database and Software: MySQL Server, Visual Studio Code / Python IDLE, and PowerPoint for the project presentation

• Hardware: Standard Windows laptop (ASUS VivoBook S14)

• (Note: AI assistance was used to help organize the GUI layout and library syntax, while I configured the physics parameters, database setup, and balance.)

How is your project creative?

Most space games rely on made-up sci-fi rules, while pure astronomy tools are often too technical for beginners. This project blends both worlds by turning real astrodynamics—including both Earth-centered Moon transfers and Sun-centered planetary transfers—into a budget-based strategy game with live animated flight paths.

As a solo developer, I focused on four key engineering factors:

• Realism vs. Playability: Keeping the physics accurate (vis-viva velocity, rocket delta-v, and Kepler's third law) while keeping the controls simple enough for anyone to play.

• Engineering Trade-Offs: Adding real penalties, such as heavier radiation shields increasing spacecraft mass and requiring more fuel.

• Environmental Hazards: Requiring thicker shielding for extreme heat near Mercury or strong radiation belts around Jupiter.

• Performance: Designing the app to run locally without needing heavy 3D graphics cards or constant internet downloads once the NASA data file is loaded.

I HOPE YOU WOULD LIKE IT
